sub_scenario.family: physical constraint versus sustained work commitment
sub_scenario.one_line: museum objects conservator: install weeks only with hourly overhead rotation

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the retouching bench and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The condition reports review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Full bench days are sustainable indefinitely with my hourly posture resets.
The resets carry the bench work.
They carry everything, really.
Someone new shadowed me in the conservation studio this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the install schedules into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
My retouching quality holds through long bench sessions only because I reset posture every hour; the neck strain log I keep shows the difference plainly.
An hourly reset, logged and proven.
Two years of log lines say so.
Short ladder tasks, an hour of mount adjustments, cost nothing.
Brief overhead work is inside the envelope.
Brief is the operative word.
I archived last cycle's notes on the condition reports and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
My physiotherapist tied the neck flare risk specifically to sustained overhead positions, not to bench work.
Overhead is the flagged posture.
Flagged in exactly those words.
A vendor call about the retouching bench ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the conservation studio checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the install schedules.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the condition reports records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
Install week on the touring exhibition meant long unbroken scaffold shifts working overhead, and by day three my neck locked so badly I handed my scalpel work to a colleague.
The overhead shifts did in three days what bench years have not.
Three days, that is all it took.
I sketched next week's plan for the install schedules before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the retouching bench updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
Two install weeks land in the spring calendar, and staffing asks for availability declarations now.
The declaration is the decision.
This form decides my spring.
I compared two options for the condition reports tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the conservation studio handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The department survey asks about my sustainable working range for install season. What does my record support writing?
